projects.name: Agent Tracking
projects.summary: Enable Themis to sync agent-side activation and project foundation with the web app, while making agent effort, progress, activity, and durable project context visible across authorized tenants.

epics.title: Agent Sync Foundation
epics.summary: Establish the authorized API and runtime foundation for syncing agent-side activation and project foundation with the web app.
epics.goal: A tenant-safe foundation exists for bidirectional agent/web synchronization without coupling the product to external tracking systems.

epics.title: Agent Activity and Progress
epics.summary: Make agent effort, progress, and activity visible in the product through a small vertical read/write experience.
epics.goal: Users can understand what agents are doing and how work is progressing from the web app.

epics.title: Durable Project Context
epics.summary: Make project context established by agents durable and visible to authorized web users.
epics.goal: Agent-established project context can be retained, retrieved, and understood as part of the product foundation.

epics.title: Zero-Knowledge Trust and Data Foundation
epics.summary: Define the zero-knowledge trust model, data classification, repository seams, and versioned cryptographic envelope contracts that constrain all later implementation.
epics.goal: The architecture has an agreed local root of trust and testable contracts proving that cloud services orchestrate ciphertext rather than hold plaintext authority.

epics.title: Local Agent Root of Trust and Vault
epics.summary: Build the themis-agent local encrypted storage and key hierarchy needed for local-first project context, credentials, and execution state.
epics.goal: A local agent can securely lock, unlock, recover, and use encrypted project data without making the cloud a plaintext authority.

epics.title: Opaque Sync and Device Security
epics.summary: Synchronize encrypted envelopes through an opaque cloud orchestrator while supporting device identity, enrollment, revocation, and client-side conflict handling.
epics.goal: Authorized devices can exchange ciphertext safely and resolve state locally without server-readable project content.

epics.title: Encrypted Product Context and Visibility Migration
epics.summary: Migrate server-readable project context and activity toward encrypted local-agent ownership, then expose approved product visibility through local-agent-mediated reads.
epics.goal: The authenticated Angular product shows authorized encrypted state without preserving server-readable context or activity as the end state.

epics.title: Capability Security and Trusted Execution
epics.summary: Define scoped sharing, capability-based access, MCP and secret-broker boundaries, local execution, and explicit external-AI trust profiles.
epics.goal: Agents and tools can act locally under explicit capabilities and trust policies without turning broad credentials or external AI into implicit authority.

epics.title: Release Supply Chain and Security Assurance
epics.summary: Harden signed releases, dependency and supply-chain review, threat-model verification, and security review for the zero-knowledge architecture.
epics.goal: The shipped agent and services can be trusted through reproducible release controls and independent security validation.

epics.title: Account WebAuthn and Passkey Authentication
epics.summary: Deliver account-level WebAuthn/passkey registration and authentication with mandatory email verification, multiple passkeys, and password fallback only after retry or explicit selection.
epics.goal: Users can register and sign in with passkeys by default while account identity, email verification/PIN, fallback behavior, session integration, and security boundaries remain explicit and distinct from PRF vault unlock and metadata APIs.

epics.title: Operational Workspace Visualization
epics.summary: Replace the authenticated Angular Projects and Dashboard surfaces with a calm, read-only operational workspace for developers and operators.
epics.goal: Authorized users can understand project identity, attention, active outcome-grouped work, validation and review confidence, and activity without KPI grids, ticket-heavy workflows, mandatory sprints, or cloud plaintext authority.

epics.title: Themis Planning Fidelity
epics.summary: Preserve approved coordinator plans through planner decomposition and complete Themis work-item contracts without losing UX research, flows, evaluation, or human-readable operational semantics.
epics.goal: Coordinator, planner, and work-item/validation guidance produce auditable, phase-complete work items whose traceability, scope changes, and validation matrices remain explicit.

epics.title: Project-Scoped Zero-Trust Themis Synchronization
epics.summary: Partition the local and cloud Themis workflow by project and synchronize encrypted project-scoped state from local agents or skills through MCP/direct API to opaque cloud transport, then notify authorized web/native clients to decrypt and materialize local read models.
epics.goal: Each Themis project scales and synchronizes independently: local agents remain the plaintext authority, cloud services authorize and relay ciphertext only, and connected clients receive project-scoped changes in real time for local ingestion and read-only visualization.

workItems.title: Define the tenant-safe agent sync contract
workItems.summary: Establish the smallest documented contract and authorization boundary for agent-side activation/project foundation updates and web reads, so later slices share stable semantics without introducing external tracker integrations.
acceptanceCriteria: The contract identifies the minimum request and response information needed for activation, project foundation, and context synchronization.
The authorization boundary identifies the tenant and project ownership checks required for agent-originated writes and web reads.
The contract defines observable handling for invalid, unauthorized, and stale/conflicting updates at a level implementers can test.
The contract is documented in the repository's existing architecture conventions and does not add an external tracking-system dependency.
scopeIn: API/gateway boundary and shared contract definitions needed by the first vertical slices
Multi-tenant authorization expectations
Versioning or conflict semantics only to the extent required by the first milestone
verificationStrategy: Run the focused Nx lint/typecheck/test targets for touched contract or API projects.
Add focused tests or contract checks covering valid, invalid, unauthorized, and stale/conflicting inputs where the existing architecture supports them.

workItems.title: Sync agent activation and project foundation
workItems.summary: Deliver a vertical write path from the agent side through the existing API/runtime boundaries into PostgreSQL-backed project foundation state, with tenant-safe authorization and a response the agent can use to confirm synchronization.
acceptanceCriteria: An authorized agent-side caller can create or update the first milestone's project foundation and activation state through the defined contract.
The write path preserves tenant and project isolation and rejects unauthorized access without leaking another tenant's state.
Successful writes are durable in the existing PostgreSQL/Drizzle data boundary or an explicitly documented existing persistence boundary.
The response communicates whether the synchronization was accepted and provides enough identity/version information for a subsequent web read.
The implementation does not add integrations with another tracking system.
scopeIn: Existing API/gateway, worker, or realtime boundaries as needed for the write path
PostgreSQL/Drizzle schema and persistence changes required for this milestone
Redis or realtime publication only when required by the existing runtime pattern
verificationStrategy: Run focused Nx lint, test, and build targets for touched backend/runtime projects.
Exercise authorized, unauthorized, create, and update cases with focused tests against the existing test strategy.
Verify persisted state through the supported application boundary rather than direct ad hoc database inspection alone.

workItems.title: Persist and retrieve durable project context
workItems.summary: Make the project context established during agent activation durable and retrievable as a coherent foundation for the web app, while keeping the first version intentionally small and tenant-safe.
acceptanceCriteria: The system stores the agreed minimum durable project context associated with the correct tenant and project.
An authorized product caller can retrieve that context through a stable application boundary.
Context retrieval distinguishes missing context from an empty or valid context according to the agreed contract.
Unauthorized callers cannot read or mutate context belonging to another tenant or project.
The first version records enough metadata to support later activity/progress interpretation without inventing a larger project-management model.

Tenant/project authorization and validation
Necessary API or shared contract updates
scopeOut: Unconfirmed context fields beyond the minimum needed for the milestone

Add tests for create/update/read, missing context, and cross-tenant or cross-project authorization failures.

workItems.summary: Give authorized product users a focused Angular view of the synchronized project foundation and durable context, completing the first agent-to-web visibility slice.

The view presents durable project context in a readable way and distinguishes loading, missing, unavailable, and error states.
The view respects tenant/project authorization and does not expose another tenant's foundation.
The UI uses the existing Angular product-app patterns and accessible interaction semantics.
The view does not require a new public Astro website surface unless an existing route or architecture decision establishes that dependency.

workItems.title: Establish Phase 0 trust model and data classification
workItems.summary: Produce the confirmed zero-knowledge threat model and classify every current and planned data flow by plaintext authority, ciphertext custody, trust boundary, retention, and recovery responsibility.
acceptanceCriteria: A Phase 0 decision record names themis-agent as the local root of trust and cloud services as ciphertext orchestrators, not plaintext authority.
Project context, activity, credentials, keys, envelopes, metadata, telemetry, and recovery data are classified with explicit allowed readers and custody.
Threat actors, compromise assumptions, recovery expectations, and explicit external-AI trust boundary are documented.
Current server-readable project context/activity is recorded as migration risk and not accepted as the target state.
Open decisions are listed rather than silently resolved, including metadata visibility, recovery actors, and product read architecture.
scopeIn: Threat model and data classification for agent, cloud, product app, MCP, secret broker, and external-AI boundaries
Migration risks from the starter implementation
Decision log for unresolved architecture choices

workItems.title: Implement opaque append-only ciphertext synchronization
workItems.summary: Provide the cloud orchestrator path that stores and relays versioned ciphertext envelopes without parsing project plaintext, using PostgreSQL for transactional authorization/index/cursor/tombstone metadata and Railway S3-compatible object storage for encrypted envelope blobs.
acceptanceCriteria: A client can append and retrieve authorized opaque envelopes through a documented cloud boundary.
Envelope payloads are stored as ciphertext-only objects in Railway S3-compatible storage; PostgreSQL stores only authorized metadata, object references, hashes, cursors, revisions, and tombstones.
The service does not require plaintext project context/activity to accept, store, or relay envelopes.
Append-only identity, ordering/cursor, duplicate, replay, retention, object-reference consistency, and tombstone behavior are documented and tested across PostgreSQL and S3 boundaries.

A real local integration run against MinIO and PostgreSQL verifies ciphertext PUT/GET, metadata-only persistence, object hash/reference consistency, and durable tombstone behavior across the configured storage boundary.
Client-side conflict handling inputs are preserved; the server does not become the source of plaintext merge authority.
Unauthorized access and tenant/workspace isolation are enforced without revealing protected content.
scopeIn: Cloud API/storage/orchestration for opaque envelopes
PostgreSQL schema and migrations for envelope metadata, authorization, cursors, revisions, tombstones, and object references
Railway S3-compatible encrypted object storage integration
Real MinIO/PostgreSQL durable integration smoke test and fixtures
Append-only cursor and envelope metadata semantics
Client-visible conflict inputs
scopeOut: Storing plaintext or encryption keys in PostgreSQL, S3, logs, queues, or realtime
verificationStrategy: [unit][required] Run focused backend/shared tests for envelope validation, cursor/order semantics, duplicate/replay handling, authorization helpers, object references, and tombstones.

workItems.title: Migrate project context and activity to encrypted ownership

Migrations remove or permanently disable plaintext columns and handle unavailable, malformed, duplicate, and partially migrated records without data leaks.
Durable tombstones are persisted transactionally so deletions and revocations cannot be undone by later synchronization or device recovery.
The plan names rollback/recovery limits and unresolved product visibility decisions.

workItems.title: Define account WebAuthn security contract and durable credential model
workItems.summary: Define account-level WebAuthn/passkey ceremonies, email verification/PIN prerequisites, retry-before-fallback behavior, multiple-credential lifecycle, session claims, and durable credential data without coupling account authentication to PRF vault unlock or metadata APIs.
acceptanceCriteria: Email is mandatory for registration and login identity; email verification/PIN completion is mandatory before a passkey credential becomes usable for account authentication.
WebAuthn is the default registration and login method; unsupported platforms or ceremony failures offer retry first, and password fallback is available only after retry or explicit user selection.
The contract supports multiple passkeys per account with stable credential IDs, labels or management metadata, last-used information, revocation/deletion semantics, and uniqueness constraints.

The durable model stores only the account-authentication credential material and required audit/session metadata; it does not store PRF vault unlock secrets, vault plaintext, or metadata API payloads.
Ceremony challenge, origin, RP ID, user verification, sign-count or equivalent clone-detection handling, expiration, replay rejection, and failure taxonomy are explicit and implementable.
The contract distinguishes account session establishment from PRF vault unlock and metadata APIs, including which later action, if any, can unlock the vault.
Ceremony validation accepts a received challenge/hash and rejects mismatches with the declared challenge_mismatch failure; tests cover the negative case.
Ceremony validation rejects revoked credentials with the declared credential_revoked failure; tests cover the negative case.
Email identity normalization is canonical, applied before lookup/storage, and covered by tests for equivalent representations.
scopeIn: WebAuthn registration and authentication ceremony contract
Account credential, challenge, verification, and session data model
Email verification/PIN prerequisite and fallback state machine
Credential lifecycle for multiple passkeys
Security and privacy boundaries between account auth, PRF vault unlock, and metadata APIs

acceptanceCriteria: A versioned, runtime-neutral materialized contract represents the complete project domain: project, epics, work items, dependencies, sprints, sprint revisions, memberships, sprint evidence, runs, run evidence, reviews, claims, status transitions, and append-only activity/timeline; no protected entity is a placeholder.

The Web implementation reads only verified project-scoped IndexedDB materialization produced by PZS-007 and never falls back to server-readable plaintext, synthetic fixtures, fabricated protected content, or an unverified projection.

Typed queries support portfolio project summaries plus project-local outcome/epic grouping, attention and blocker derivation, work detail, dependency navigation, optional sprint context, validation/evidence confidence, runs, reviews, claims, transitions, and chronological activity.

Human-readable state/event translation explains what changed, who or what acted, why attention is needed, what evidence/review exists or is missing, and the next safe local action while retaining stable source event identity and provenance.

Visible, loading, empty, locked, unavailable, stale, corrupt, quota-limited, resyncing, error, unauthorized, review-pending, accepted, rejected, rework, deleted, and no-sprint states are explicit, accessible to consumers, and never imply cloud/local authority that does not exist.
Incremental IndexedDB updates, snapshot rebuilds, tombstones, schema upgrades, duplicate/out-of-order delivery, and full resync yield deterministic query results and preserve cross-entity references.
Project/tenant/device scope is validated on every query; one project's corruption, lock, quota, or rebuild cannot block or leak another project's materialization.
Compatibility/versioning, redaction, staleness, failure, and recovery semantics are documented, and raw HTTP/WebSocket/server artifacts contain no protected read-model plaintext.

Real API/OpenAPI and composed gateway tests verify only opaque envelope/metadata boundaries; Angular adapter tests consume verified IndexedDB and exercise every complete materialized state without mutation affordances.
The existing rich operational flows, progressive disclosure inputs, accessibility semantics, and no-sprint usefulness remain supported rather than replaced by generic project-management language.

Real evidence proves the adapter and app consume verified IndexedDB materialization from real PZS-007 synchronization, with real API, app, gateway, and security artifacts; synthetic fixtures may be used only as explicitly negative malformed-test inputs and never as completion evidence.

workItems.title: Close production zero-knowledge security control blockers
workItems.summary: Implement the remaining cross-cutting controls that prevent the existing zero-knowledge proof from being treated as production-safe: verifiable capability signatures with key custody/revocation, authenticated local-agent visibility transport, protected-data classification and audit enforcement, bounded external-AI policy, safe runtime redaction, and nonce/key lifecycle invariants.
acceptanceCriteria: Capability signatures are cryptographically verified against an issuer key, scoped to the signed payload, and rejected when forged, expired, revoked, replayed, or issued by an unknown key; production key custody, rotation, and compromise revocation are durable and documented.

MCP and execution outputs classify protected plaintext separately from internal/public data and deny protected projections by default unless a named provider, field projection, purpose, retention, consent record, and local output validation satisfy policy.

Runtime errors, audit events, telemetry, and release diagnostics emit stable redacted classes and correlation IDs without protected plaintext, secrets, raw challenges, or keys; vault nonce/key lifecycle invariants are enforced rather than proof-only.
Focused implementation and security evidence closes or explicitly blocks each mapped finding without accepting a critical finding as risk; no external AI provider or mobile client is introduced.

workItems.title: Define the project-scoped synchronization architecture and assurance model
workItems.summary: Specify the P0/P11 contract that partitions Themis by project, preserves local plaintext authority, constrains cloud services to opaque project-scoped transport, and establishes threat, performance, compatibility, and deferred-native decisions before implementation.
acceptanceCriteria: A versioned architecture contract defines independently loadable local project stores and independently authorized cloud streams, with project identity, opaque envelope, cursor, revision, idempotency, tombstone, snapshot, checkpoint, notification, and client-materialization semantics.

The complete projected domain is mapped: project, epics, work items, dependencies, sprints, sprint revisions, memberships, sprint evidence, runs, run evidence, reviews, claims, status transitions, and append-only activity/timeline; raw .themis files, filesystem paths, keys, secrets, and plaintext protected content are forbidden from transport.

Trust and authority diagrams state that local agents/skills remain plaintext and mutation authority; cloud services only authorize, persist ciphertext, assign non-sensitive cursor/revision metadata, and signal availability, and never decrypt, index plaintext, merge domain state, or become project authority.

The threat model covers cross-project/tenant/device confusion, metadata disclosure, replay/rollback, stale cursors, tombstone resurrection, malicious or malformed envelopes, notification spoofing, quota abuse, denial of service, compromised clients, logs/telemetry, and recovery.

The performance model defines measurable project-count, event-volume, envelope-size, materialization-latency, reconnect, compaction, storage, quota, and independent-failure budgets with representative scale fixtures and pass/fail thresholds.

Migration compatibility and rollback decisions explain how global state becomes project stores without destructive cutover or authority inversion; existing ZK-006, SEC-001, SYNC-001, ZK-020, and ZK-022 are cited only as foundations, not evidence that local-Themis synchronization is complete.

P11 is explicitly mapped: runtime-neutral contracts/adapters may support future native clients, but native UI/runtime implementation, delivery, and native-specific key storage are first-milestone non-goals.

The phase inventory P0-P11 and update-vs-create rationale are machine-checkable by scripts/plan-fidelity.test.ts without omitting UX flows, human-readable event/state translation, validation, or deferred-native scope.
scopeIn: Architecture decision records and versioned runtime-neutral contracts for project stores, publishers, opaque API/realtime, client sync, and materialization
Threat, metadata-disclosure, recovery, migration/rollback, performance/SLO, quota, and compatibility models

workItems.title: Migrate global Themis state into isolated project stores
workItems.summary: Deliver a reversible, observable P1 migration from the global Themis planning/state bottleneck to independently loadable project stores while preserving append-only history, identities, relationships, and local mutation authority.
acceptanceCriteria: A migration inventories every global record and assigns it to exactly one project store or an explicitly quarantined/unassigned class; no entity, dependency, sprint membership, evidence, review, transition, or timeline event is silently dropped.
Project stores can be loaded, validated, backed up, restored, and synchronized independently without reading unrelated project domain state.
The migration preserves stable IDs, ordering, append-only activity, dependency references, sprint/revision/membership relations, claims, statuses, run/review evidence, and tombstones.

Dry-run, resumable cutover, crash recovery, mixed-version compatibility window, and idempotent rerun are observable; pre-cutover backups and checksums support rollback without accepting post-cutover writes into both authorities.
Rollback and forward-recovery rules prevent split-brain mutation authority and reject stale global-state replay after project-store activation.
Cross-project references are rejected or represented by an explicit non-protected reference contract; moving or deleting one project cannot corrupt another.
No raw .themis file, local path, secret, or key is emitted to cloud or logs; migration remains local and preserves plaintext authority.
A representative multi-project fixture proves one corrupt or oversized project does not prevent healthy project stores from loading or migrating.
scopeIn: Local state/event partitioning, migration ledger, compatibility reader, backup/restore, cutover and rollback
Complete current Themis domain and relationship preservation
Project-level validation and independent failure isolation
verificationStrategy: [unit][required] `pnpm themis:test`; evidence: the existing project-less local workflow suite passes migration fixtures for complete-domain preservation, idempotent rerun, crash resume, corrupt project, stale replay, and rollback.

[app-e2e][not-applicable] No Angular route or browser behavior changes.
[gateway-e2e][not-applicable] No gateway, worker, or realtime composition changes.
[site-e2e][not-applicable] No public Astro route changes.

workItems.title: Extract the reusable project-scoped local core and explicit workspace registry
workItems.summary: Deliver the P2 local core that opens, validates, mutates, snapshots, and observes one registered project at a time, with explicit user registration of workspace roots/projects and no recursive disk scanning.
acceptanceCriteria: A real reusable `themis-workflow` Nx library is created and exposes project-scoped runtime-neutral operations for the complete Themis domain, dependency validation, claims/status transitions, append-only events, snapshots, and project-local cursors without loading unrelated projects.
The workspace registry requires explicit user registration, update, disable, and removal of roots/projects; it never recursively scans disks or infers projects from arbitrary descendants.
Registry records minimize local path exposure, never enter encrypted cloud envelopes or notification metadata, and clearly separate local locator data from portable project identity.

Concurrent opens and mutations enforce one project authority and deterministic append ordering; corruption, lock contention, unknown project, moved root, and partially migrated store produce bounded actionable errors.
One project's failure, lock, size, or malformed event cannot block listing, opening, or mutating another registered project.
CLI, OpenCode tools, local agent, MCP skills, publisher, and future native runtimes consume the same `themis-workflow` core without embedding Node filesystem assumptions in portable contracts.
Human-readable translation maps domain status transitions and low-level events to stable activity semantics while retaining raw local audit identity and append-only provenance.
Migration compatibility consumes PZS-002 output and rejects legacy global fallback after project activation except through the explicit rollback procedure.

The implementation explicitly migrates the CLI and OpenCode adapters onto the real `themis-workflow` Nx library rather than leaving parallel project-core logic or compatibility shims as the delivered path.

Verification demonstrates complete-domain coverage, explicit registry-only discovery, no recursive scanning, deterministic concurrency, project isolation, path redaction, and PZS-002 compatibility through Nx targets and the existing `pnpm themis:test` command.
P11 remains runtime-neutral: native UI/runtime delivery and native-specific key storage are explicitly deferred and are not represented as completed implementation.

workItems.title: Publish encrypted project changes through the packaged CLI, MCP, and direct API
workItems.summary: Deliver P3 publisher adapters and the packaged `npx @visomi/themis sync` command so an initialized OpenCode-produced `.themis` workspace can transform committed project-scoped logical state into locally encrypted snapshots/events, publish pending deltas through MCP or direct API, and report an observable, resumable sync outcome without surrendering local mutation or plaintext authority.
acceptanceCriteria: From the root of an initialized `.themis` workspace produced through OpenCode, `npx @visomi/themis sync` resolves the explicit workspace registry and, by default, attempts every enabled registered project; project filters are explicit overrides, disabled/unregistered projects are not synchronized, and no recursive filesystem scan or implicit descendant discovery occurs.

For each selected project, the command reads the reusable project-scoped logical state contract from PZS-003, never packages or uploads raw `.themis` files, local paths, keys, secrets, or plaintext domain values, and locally transforms committed project state into canonical encrypted snapshots/events.

A committed local project event or snapshot can be selected by project cursor and published through equivalent MCP and direct-API adapters using the canonical project-scoped envelope contract; transport framing differences are explicitly documented and request/acknowledgement hashes prove contract equivalence.

Publication occurs only after local commit, never makes cloud acknowledgement the mutation authority, and records project-local outbox, cursor, acknowledgement, and retry state so subsequent runs are idempotent, delta-only, and do not duplicate domain mutations or already acknowledged envelopes.

The packaged command delegates browser authentication, remote project create/link decisions, and CLI/browser enrollment/pairing to PZS-011, then resumes the same correlation-safe run after the browser callback without accepting tokens, project authority, or plaintext from an untrusted origin.

The terminal presents stable human-readable states for registry validation, authentication handoff, remote create/link/pairing, local encryption, pending-delta publication, retry/backoff, per-project completion, partial completion, offline deferral, and final URL handoff; low-level events and error codes remain available for audit without exposing protected values.

Offline, timeout, browser cancellation, interrupted callback, partial batch, duplicate acknowledgement, stale cursor, quota/backpressure, revoked capability/device, malformed server response, and process interruption remain recoverable and observable per project; rerunning resumes from durable project-local outbox/bootstrap state.

A failed, paused, locked, corrupt, or offline project does not block local work or synchronization of another enabled project; the command exits with an actionable aggregate result that distinguishes complete, partial, deferred/offline, authentication-required, retryable, and terminal failures.

After successful publication/bootstrap the command prints and, when supported, opens the canonical authenticated Angular app URL supplied by PZS-011; the URL contains no protected plaintext, local path, key, secret, or bearer credential and identifies the authorized project through an opaque safe route identifier.

MCP calls expose narrowly scoped publish/status/resync operations and cannot recursively discover workspaces, bypass the explicit registry, broaden project capabilities, or mutate local domain state outside the approved local workflow authority.

Adversarial registry, capability, path, plaintext, replay, scope-escalation, callback-correlation, malformed-response, and URL-disclosure checks fail closed across packaged CLI, MCP, and direct API paths.
P11 native runtime delivery remains a non-goal; the packaged Node CLI and publisher contracts remain runtime-neutral at shared seams.

workItems.title: Persist and authorize opaque project streams in the API
workItems.summary: Deliver P4 cloud API behavior that authorizes project-scoped publishers/readers, persists opaque snapshots/events, assigns monotonic cursor/revision metadata, and remains zero-knowledge and non-authoritative for domain state.
acceptanceCriteria: Authenticated HTTP endpoints append and fetch project snapshots/events using opaque envelopes and explicit project authorization, tenant/device/capability checks, idempotency keys, cursors, revisions, object hashes, and tombstone metadata.
PostgreSQL/object storage contains only the approved metadata allowlist and ciphertext; the API cannot decrypt, parse/index protected domain fields, merge domain state, or decide domain conflicts.

Create/fetch/list/checkpoint semantics reject cross-project, cross-tenant, revoked, malformed, oversized, duplicate-conflict, stale-base, replay, rollback, and unsupported-version inputs without disclosure.
Cursors/revisions are monotonic within one project stream but independent across projects; concurrent appends are transactional and one project's contention or failure cannot block another.
Snapshot plus incremental fetch returns a verifiable recovery chain and bounded page semantics without transferring raw .themis files or local filesystem locators.
Tombstones and checkpoint references remain durable and cannot be bypassed by replaying older envelopes; server retention never silently discards the only recoverable chain.

Errors, metrics, traces, audits, and object names use safe routing/correlation metadata and never include ciphertext-derived plaintext, keys, secrets, raw local paths, or protected IDs beyond the approved allowlist.
OpenAPI documents every success/error response and runtime-neutral clients can consume it without server domain-state knowledge.

PZS-005 provides a reproducible real-evidence harness that starts isolated API/PostgreSQL/MinIO, creates real device authorization, generates a unique runId and streamId, executes authenticated real HTTP calls, captures every request/response at transport, captures same-run PostgreSQL/MinIO state, logs, traces/metrics or current-run explicit N/A proof, generates HAR/JUnit/OpenAPI, and fails if artifacts are synthetic, missing, unrelated, or from another run.

Every required case maps caseId, runId, streamId, safe request method/path/body, observed status/code/body, correlationId, HAR, JUnit, raw HTTP, acceptance criterion, and artifact hash/path: authorized append 201; duplicate 200; duplicate conflict; authorized fetch; cross-project; cross-tenant; revoked device; un-enrolled device; malformed; oversized; unsupported version; stale base; rollback; replay; valid checkpoint; checkpoint hash mismatch; valid recovery; missing checkpoint; pruned cursor; tombstone; tombstone resurrection; retention boundary; and device lifecycle.
The stale-base case rejects with HTTP 409 and opaque_envelope_rejected; pruned or invalid cursors never return silent 200 empty and instead return documented recovery behavior.

Same-run concrete evidence includes DB rows, object metadata and blob hash, sync-specific HTTP, server logs, trace/metric output or explicit current-run N/A proof, and disclosure scan; generated OpenAPI includes every in-scope sync/device/checkpoint/recovery success and error response.
Evidence is tracked under `docs/verification/<run>` rather than ignored dist-only paths, and the full eight-category matrix plus literal P0-P11 phase/item/status/gap matrix is retained.
Existing generic ZK-006/E2E evidence is explicitly non-substitutive and cannot satisfy this PZS-005 gate.

OpenAPI, safe observability, transaction and project-isolation behavior
scopeOut: Server decryption, plaintext indexing, domain merge, project mutation authority

workItems.title: Signal project change availability over authenticated realtime channels
workItems.summary: Deliver P5 authenticated WebSocket/realtime notifications that announce safe project-scoped cursor availability without carrying encrypted payloads, protected content, or domain authority.
acceptanceCriteria: An authorized client subscribes to explicitly authorized project streams and receives notification metadata containing only approved project routing alias, latest cursor/revision, checkpoint hint, event kind, and correlation/time fields.
Notifications never contain ciphertext envelopes, plaintext domain content, local paths, keys, secrets, entity titles/descriptions, evidence, or human-readable activity.
Subscription, reconnect, token refresh, revocation, project removal, stale session, cross-tenant/project guessing, and unauthorized channel joins fail closed without existence disclosure.

Publication is best-effort availability signaling, not state transfer or ordering authority; clients always fetch and verify envelopes through PZS-005 and tolerate duplicate, delayed, missing, and out-of-order notifications.
Reconnect resumes from a client-held project cursor, detects gaps/staleness, and triggers bounded fetch/resync without replaying protected data through realtime.
Backpressure/coalescing is project-scoped; a noisy, over-quota, or disconnected project cannot starve notifications for another authorized project.
Safe logs/metrics identify channel health using allowlisted metadata only and preserve project/tenant isolation.
A composed gateway test proves API append causes the correct authorized notification and no notification for unauthorized or unrelated projects.

Verification uses real authenticated WebSocket frames emitted by a real append through PZS-005, not synthetic frames: capture raw frames, handshake/auth results, correlation IDs, server logs, reconnect/gap/revocation outcomes, and metadata-only payload assertions.

Real scenarios cover per-project authorization, reconnect and cursor-gap recovery, revoked device/session, cross-project and cross-tenant denial, noisy-neighbor/backpressure isolation, duplicate/out-of-order notifications, and disclosure scans over raw frames/logs.

workItems.title: Build the runtime-neutral client sync engine and Web IndexedDB materializer
workItems.summary: Deliver P6/P11 client infrastructure that fetches opaque project snapshots/events, decrypts and validates locally, deterministically merges them, and transactionally materializes a Web IndexedDB query database through runtime-neutral contracts.
acceptanceCriteria: A runtime-neutral state machine subscribes to metadata notifications, fetches snapshot plus incremental envelopes per project, verifies project/cursor/revision/hash/version, decrypts through an injected local crypto adapter, and never exposes keys or plaintext to cloud services.

Deterministic merge covers the complete projected domain, dependencies and append-only activity; identical valid envelope sets yield identical query state regardless of duplicate delivery or permitted fetch batching.

Web IndexedDB stores client-local materialized project data, sync cursor/checkpoint, tombstones, schema version, staleness/error state, and rebuild metadata transactionally; no server plaintext query fallback exists.

Startup, foreground refresh, reconnect, notification gap, offline queue, stale cursor, partial transaction, malformed envelope, unsupported version, locked key, quota exhaustion, rollback/replay, tombstone, corruption, and full resync are observable per project.
One project's lock, corruption, quota, resync, or schema upgrade cannot block another project's local query database.

Adapters are runtime-neutral and avoid IndexedDB/DOM/Node assumptions in core contracts; Web IndexedDB is the only first-milestone materializer, while native runtime/UI/key-store implementation remains explicitly deferred under P11.
Materialization preserves stable IDs and references across project, epics, work items, dependencies, sprints/revisions/memberships/evidence, runs/evidence, reviews, claims/transitions, and timeline.

Client logs/errors use safe codes and correlation metadata; raw ciphertext may be retained only in the encrypted sync cache, while decrypted projections remain client-local and never enter URLs, cloud telemetry, or reports.

Verification uses a real runtime-neutral sync engine and real Web IndexedDB with two projects and two browser/client profiles; an actual notification from a real append triggers fetch, local decryption/validation, and materialization.

Verification proves deterministic manifest equality, transactional rebuild/tombstone/schema upgrade, offline/reconnect/stale/corrupt/quota/resync isolation, and that no server plaintext fallback is invoked. Native remains a non-goal.

workItems.title: Implement project snapshots, compaction, checkpoints, and recovery
workItems.summary: Deliver the P9 lifecycle that bounds each project's stream through verifiable snapshots/checkpoints and supports stale detection, resync, corruption recovery, and tombstone-safe compaction without cloud plaintext authority.
acceptanceCriteria: Authorized local publishers create encrypted project snapshots at defined event/size thresholds and append checkpoint metadata that binds project, covered cursor/revision, snapshot hash, predecessor, schema/envelope versions, and tombstone horizon.
Cloud compaction operates only on opaque retention/checkpoint metadata and never decrypts, merges domain state, or discards envelopes needed by the declared recovery window.
Clients verify checkpoint chains, bootstrap from snapshot plus incremental events, detect stale/missing/pruned/corrupt chains, and choose bounded incremental catch-up or full resync.
Replay of an older snapshot/checkpoint, cursor rollback, forked chain, missing tombstone horizon, hash mismatch, unsupported version, and tombstone resurrection fail closed.

Recovery covers interrupted snapshot upload, checkpoint published before object visibility, partial local materialization, corrupted IndexedDB, lost cursor, restored old backup, pruned cursor, and project deletion.
Retention and recovery guarantees are explicit and observable; destructive compaction cannot occur until recoverability conditions and client compatibility windows are met.
Recovery and compaction execute independently per project and preserve local plaintext/mutation authority.
Long-history fixtures prove bounded bootstrap time/storage and equivalence between full replay and snapshot-plus-incremental materialization.

A real encrypted snapshot/checkpoint upload and recovery run captures durable PostgreSQL rows, MinIO object metadata/blob hashes, chain/tombstone bindings, and client recovery results under one run identity.

Real failure scenarios cover interrupted upload/object delay, corrupt database, old backup, pruned cursor, full resync, compaction safety, and replay equivalence; every artifact is durable, hash-addressed, and non-synthetic.

workItems.title: Bootstrap browser authentication, remote project linking, and device pairing for CLI sync
workItems.summary: Deliver the separate P3 browser-bootstrap sub-scope used by `npx @visomi/themis sync`: open an account-authenticated browser journey, make explicit authorized cloud project create/link decisions, enroll and pair the CLI and browser devices without cloud plaintext or key custody, resume the originating CLI run safely, and provide the canonical Angular handoff URL.
acceptanceCriteria: Starting from an initialized OpenCode-produced `.themis` workspace, the CLI creates a short-lived, single-use, correlation-bound bootstrap request and opens the system browser to the existing Angular account-authentication boundary; a manual URL is printed when browser launch is unavailable.

The browser flow uses the existing PASSKEY-002/PASSKEY-003 account session behavior, clearly separates account authentication from vault/project-key unlock, and returns only a one-time authorization result to the originating CLI callback; bearer credentials, passkey material, vault keys, and protected project plaintext never appear in URLs, terminal output, logs, or cloud project metadata.

Bootstrap accepts only projects selected from the explicit PZS-003 registry and never recursively scans the workspace, parent directories, descendants, sibling repositories, or arbitrary disk locations.

For each enabled registered local project, the browser presents an explicit create/link decision based on stable portable project identity and the authorized tenant: no authorized remote match can create a new remote project, one exact authorized match can be linked after confirmation, and ambiguous, conflicting, cross-tenant, deleted, or unauthorized matches fail closed with actionable choices rather than silently linking.

Creating or linking a remote project establishes only opaque project identity, authorization, routing, and allowed metadata; it never uploads raw `.themis` files, local paths, keys, secrets, or plaintext project/domain values and never makes the remote project the local mutation authority.

The flow enrolls or reuses a durable CLI device identity through the existing ZK-007/PZS-005 device lifecycle, pairs the authenticated browser device to the same authorized project, and distributes/wraps project access material only client-side so the cloud cannot decrypt, unwrap, or impersonate either device.

Pairing visibly identifies the requesting CLI device and affected project aliases using safe user-recognizable data, requires explicit browser confirmation, rejects mismatched correlation/origin/session/tenant/project/device claims, expires outstanding requests, and supports cancellation and revocation without existence disclosure.

The bootstrap state machine is durable and idempotent: rerunning after browser close, process interruption, callback loss, already-created remote project, already-linked project, or already-enrolled/paired devices resumes or safely reuses prior results without duplicate remote projects, duplicate enrollments, authority inversion, or lost local work.

Human-readable CLI/browser states and errors cover opening browser, waiting for authentication, authentication required, choosing create/link, awaiting pairing confirmation, enrolled, linked, cancelled, expired, revoked, ambiguous match, unauthorized, offline/deferred, resumable, and complete; low-level safe codes and correlation IDs remain available for audit.

When bootstrap succeeds, it returns to PZS-004 a scoped publication capability and canonical authenticated Angular project/workspace URL; the URL uses an opaque safe route identifier, contains no bearer token or protected/local data, and lands on the PZS-007/THM-OWV materialized project state when available.

Offline or unavailable cloud/auth services leave local work authoritative and usable, preserve a resumable bootstrap record, and do not mark unsent project changes synchronized; one project's failed create/link/pairing does not block bootstrap or later sync for another enabled project.

Negative checks cover callback interception, CSRF/state substitution, loopback binding, origin/RP/session mismatch, replay, expired request, device impersonation, cross-tenant/project link, ambiguous identity, revoked device, unsafe URL, metadata disclosure, recursive scan attempts, and raw `.themis`/plaintext upload; every case fails closed.
P11 native runtime and native key storage remain non-goals; shared bootstrap and pairing contracts remain runtime-neutral while this item delivers the Node CLI plus Angular browser flow only.

evidence.summary: Canonical Ed25519 proof decoding and HTTP regression
evidence.value: Changed apps/web/api/src/capabilities/capability-router.ts to require base64url decode/re-encode canonical equality before verification, rejecting alternate trailing-bit encodings; changed apps/web/api/src/capabilities/capability-router.spec.ts to tamper only unused trailing bits and assert 401 capability_unauthenticated. Valid enrolled Ed25519 negotiation, DeviceIdentityStore enrollment/revocation, and isolation fixtures remain unchanged.

Ed25519 signatures are 64 bytes, encoded as 86 base64url characters. The final character contains unused low bits; mutating those bits can produce a different proof string that Buffer.from(..., 'base64url') decodes to the identical 64-byte signature. The prior verifier authenticated decoded bytes without enforcing a canonical wire representation, allowing the tampered HTTP proof to receive 200. Canonical round-trip validation now fails closed.
